title: Ashtavakra's answer
hookLine: a king asks how to be free, and the sage says: right now
carry: you are the witness, free right now
tomorrow: The tiger who thought he was a goat

cards: Back in King Janaka's palace. The king who has everything sits before a young sage bent in eight places and asks: how do I know, how am I free, how do I let go?
In the old stories, a seeker who asks that gets a long program. Twelve years in a forest. A thousand rules.
A ladder with a hundred rungs. Ashtavakra starts gently. Then, a few verses in, he says something so bold you may read it twice.

teach.h: SENSES AS POISON, VIRTUES AS NECTAR.
teach.b: Here's the opening of the reply, paraphrased. If you want freedom, my child, treat the pull of the senses like poison, and drink forgiveness, honesty, kindness, contentment and truth like nectar.
The next verse turns everything. You are not earth.

teach.h: YOU ARE NOT EARTH, WATER, FIRE.
teach.b: You are not water, or fire, or air, or space. To be free, know yourself as the witness of all these: awareness itself. The five elements that make up everything, and you're none of them.
You're the one they appear to. Then the verse that stops people. If you set the body aside and rest in awareness, then right now, this very moment, you'll be happy, at peace, and free.
Not after twelve years. Now. A little later he adds: right and wrong, pleasure and pain, belong to the mind, not to you.
You're not the doer, not the one who enjoys the results. You were always free.
This is the Hindu teaching of the sakshi, the witness: the self watches body and mind and is never caught by them.

teach.h: RIGHT NOW: HAPPY, AT PEACE, FREE.
teach.b: Is that too easy? Teachers say it's simple, not easy. Nothing has to be built.
But everything you keep counting as yourself has to be seen through, the way the leader by the river had to stop counting and turn around. The Ashtavakra Gita doesn't give you a ladder.
It points at the floor you're already standing on. So the night before a big test, the panic is real, and it's seen. You are the one seeing it.

how: Students of the Ashtavakra Gita often chant or read its first chapter slowly, pausing on each verse, and use its list of the five elements as a contemplation: noticing each as known, and resting as the knower.

o: knowing yourself as the witness, free right now
a long ladder of rules that frees you at the end
reaching heaven through years of strict effort

s: Ashtavakra tells Janaka freedom takes many lifetimes of effort
he says: rest in awareness, and right now you'll be happy, at peace and free.
the Ashtavakra Gita begins with ethical advice
it starts by urging forgiveness, honesty, kindness, contentment and truth.
teachers of the text say its teaching is easy
they say simple, not easy: nothing is built, but everything must be seen through.

games.q: you're King Janaka. the sage names earth, water, fire, air and space, the stuff of everything. which one does he say you are?
o: none of them: you're their witness.
games.why: none. you are the witness of all these, awareness itself, he says, and resting there you're free right now.

practice: Walk Ashtavakra's list slowly: earth, the weight of the body on the seat; water, the moisture in the mouth; fire, the warmth of the skin; air, the breath; space, the room around you, each one noticed, none of them what you are.
Then, for a few breaths, rest as the one noticing, right now. If the mind says it's not working, that's a thought too: noticed.

wordCard.voice: Jnana yoga, in the Ashtavakra Gita's answer: you are not the elements, but the witness of them, awareness itself; rest there, and you're free now.

orig.note: Sanskrit: sakshi, the witness; what the Ashtavakra Gita and Vedanta call pure awareness.

carryVoice: Your line: you are the witness, free right now. Not earth, not water, not fire: the one they appear to. That's day two seventy-nine.

sources.ref: Ashtavakra Gita 1.2–1.4 (poison and nectar; not the five elements; the witness; free now)
Ashtavakra Gita 1.6 (not the doer, not the enjoyer)
